title: Episode 261: 🇳🇱 C++ Under the Sea 🇳🇱 Bernhard, Koen & C++26 Reflection!

sentences.en: Frost has this very algorithmic-oriented style of, like, it works with iterators, it composes into different algorithms, right?
sentences.zh: Thrust 的风格非常偏向算法，比如它使用迭代器，并将其组合成不同的算法，对吧？

sentences.en: So, like, some algorithms are implemented in terms of other algorithms, and it has this nice touch, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，有些算法是基于其他算法实现的，这种设计很巧妙，对吧？

sentences.en: Whereas when you go into CUB, it's just full of, like, C-style cars reinterpreting, type-aliasing.
sentences.zh: 而当你深入 CUB 时，里面全是 C 风格的类型转换和类型别名。

sentences.en: It has, like, every kind of UB that you can imagine, which is why I think CUB actually stands for CUDA Undefined Behavior, right?
sentences.zh: 它包含了你能想象到的各种未定义行为（UB），所以我认为 CUB 其实代表 CUDA Undefined Behavior（CUDA 未定义行为），对吧？

sentences.en: No, it's, CUB is specific to our platform, which means it's not, like, we NVIDIA make the platform.
sentences.zh: 不，CUB 是我们平台特有的，这意味着 NVIDIA 制造了这个平台。

sentences.en: Yeah, the parrot thing, well, just, I am now, I have a second daughter now, and as things go, I can make a lot of dad jokes now, so Sean Parrott.
sentences.zh: 关于鹦鹉那个梗，嗯，我刚有了第二个女儿，按照惯例，我现在能讲很多冷笑话了，所以叫 Sean Parrott。

sentences.en: Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 恭喜。

sentences.en: There's a conversation to be had at a later date about API design and the importance of an ergonomic and intuitive interface.
sentences.zh: 关于 API 设计以及符合人体工程学和直观界面的重要性，我们以后可以再找时间讨论。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 261, recorded on October 10th, 2025.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客，第 261 期，录制于 2025 年 10 月 10 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host, Bryce, we continue our conversation live from C++ under the sea in the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天和我的联合主持人 Bryce 一起，继续我们在荷兰“C++ 海底世界”活动的现场对话。

sentences.en: In this episode, we chat with Bernhard, a fellow NVIDIA from Austria, Kuhn from Belgium for the third time, C++ 26 Reflection, and more.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们与来自奥地利的 NVIDIA 同事 Bernhard，以及第三次做客的来自比利时的 Kuhn 聊聊 C++ 26 反射等话题。

sentences.en: Hello, NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 你好，NVIDIA。

sentences.en: Oh, hi.
sentences.zh: 哦，嗨。

sentences.en: Use yourself.
sentences.zh: 介绍一下你自己。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Can you also explain how a great extortation is?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下什么是伟大的勒索吗？

sentences.en: Oh, no, I'm not explaining that, because I might get it wrong.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，我不能解释，因为我可能会说错。

sentences.en: I have to check up how it works again.
sentences.zh: 我得再去查查它是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: Okay, my name is Bernhard.
sentences.zh: 好的，我叫 Bernhard。

sentences.en: I joined NVIDIA one and a half years ago.
sentences.zh: 我加入 NVIDIA 一年半了。

sentences.en: I started out in Cobb, but since then, I think I took over maintaining Frost as well, and I have my hands in Libcoo++, and I think by now I kind of do everything right.
sentences.zh: 我最初是在 CUB 组，但从那以后，我想我也接手了 Thrust 的维护工作，我还参与了 Libcu++，我想现在我基本上什么都做，对吧？

sentences.en: He's an everything man, folks.
sentences.zh: 各位，他是个全能选手。

sentences.en: He does everything.
sentences.zh: 他什么都做。

sentences.en: What do you like better, Cobb or Thrust?
sentences.zh: 你更喜欢哪一个，CUB 还是 Thrust？

sentences.en: Ooh, good question.
sentences.zh: 噢，好问题。

sentences.en: They have very different styles.
sentences.zh: 它们的风格非常不同。

sentences.en: What I like about FroSt...
sentences.zh: 我喜欢 Thrust 的地方在于……

sentences.en: He dodged the question, folks.
sentences.zh: 各位，他回避了这个问题。

sentences.en: Well done.
sentences.zh: 干得漂亮。

sentences.en: You're a future politician.
sentences.zh: 你是个未来的政客。

sentences.en: So, Frost has this very algorithmic-oriented style of, like, it works with iterators.
sentences.zh: 所以，Thrust 的风格非常偏向算法，比如它使用迭代器。

sentences.en: It composes into different algorithms, right?
sentences.zh: 它将其组合成不同的算法，对吧？

sentences.en: So, like, some algorithms are implemented in terms of other algorithms, and it has this nice touch, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，有些算法是基于其他算法实现的，这种设计很巧妙，对吧？

sentences.en: Whereas when you go into Cobb, it's just full of, like, C-style cars reinterpreting, type-aliasing.
sentences.zh: 而当你深入 CUB 时，里面全是 C 风格的类型转换和类型别名。

sentences.en: It has, like, every kind of UB that you can imagine, which is why I think Cobb actually stands for CUDA Undefined Behavior, right?
sentences.zh: 它包含了你能想象到的各种未定义行为（UB），所以我认为 CUB 其实代表 CUDA Undefined Behavior（CUDA 未定义行为），对吧？

sentences.en: It's...
sentences.zh: 它是……

sentences.en: Cub is specific to our platform, which means it's not on...
sentences.zh: CUB 是我们平台特有的，这意味着它不是在……

sentences.en: Like, we, NVIDIA, make the platform.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们 NVIDIA 制造了这个平台。

sentences.en: Cub is the implementation.
sentences.zh: CUB 是实现方案。

sentences.en: And so we're allowed to do...
sentences.zh: 所以我们被允许做……

sentences.en: Like, look, if you're within the standard library, the standard library implementer is allowed to do whatever they want.
sentences.zh: 你看，如果你在标准库内部，标准库的实现者可以随心所欲。

sentences.en: It's not UB because you're the standard library.
sentences.zh: 那不是未定义行为，因为你是标准库。

sentences.en: You better not do anything that's going to break.
sentences.zh: 你最好别做任何会导致崩溃的事情。

sentences.en: But Cub is...
sentences.zh: 但 CUB 是……

sentences.en: It only runs on our platform, which...
sentences.zh: 它只在我们的平台上运行，这……

sentences.en: And it's provided by the vendor, which means there's no UB in Cub.
sentences.zh: 而且它是由供应商提供的，这意味着 CUB 中没有未定义行为。

sentences.en: It's all juSt...
sentences.zh: 这完全是……

sentences.en: Like, the only thing that Cub might have is some undocumented behavior about how it works.
sentences.zh: CUB 可能唯一有的就是一些关于其工作原理的未记录行为。

sentences.en: But I do think that the Cub block-level primitives can be very nice to work with.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为 CUB 的块级原语非常好用。

sentences.en: They're very nice abstraction.
sentences.zh: 它们是非常好的抽象。

sentences.en: They're very nice on the outside.
sentences.zh: 从外部看它们非常棒。

sentences.en: Just don't, you know, have to look on the inside.
sentences.zh: 只是你不需要去深究内部实现。

sentences.en: But, yeah.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的。

sentences.en: What does Cub...
sentences.zh: CUB 代表什么……

sentences.en: I mean, that's really not what Cub stands for, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，那真的不是 CUB 的含义，对吧？

sentences.en: I assume not.
sentences.zh: 我想不是。

sentences.en: It's Cuda Unbound.
sentences.zh: 它是 Cuda Unbound。

sentences.en: Yeah, Cuda Unbound.
sentences.zh: 是的，Cuda Unbound。

sentences.en: Okay, Cuda Unbound.
sentences.zh: 好的，Cuda Unbound。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What were you saying the joke was?
sentences.zh: 你刚才说的那个笑话是什么？

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你什么意思？

sentences.en: You missed the joke?
sentences.zh: 你没听懂那个笑话？

sentences.en: Yeah, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我没听懂。

sentences.en: What was the joke?
sentences.zh: 那个笑话是什么？

sentences.en: Oh, the joke was that I think Cub could stand for Cuda Undefined Behavior because it contains so much of that.
sentences.zh: 哦，笑话是我认为 CUB 可以代表 CUDA Undefined Behavior，因为它包含太多那种东西了。

sentences.en: But I fully agree with Bryce's analysis before that because we know the tool chain that Cub runs on, right?
sentences.zh: 但我完全同意 Bryce 之前的分析，因为我们了解 CUB 运行的工具链，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, we know the NVCC versions, the process Cub.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们了解 NVCC 版本，了解处理 CUB 的过程。

sentences.en: We know, like, the behavior of our compiler.
sentences.zh: 我们了解编译器的行为。

sentences.en: So we have leeway in what we can write there because we know how the compiler processes and translates our code.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在编写代码时有回旋余地，因为我们知道编译器是如何处理和转换我们的代码的。

sentences.en: And the biggest problem, like, the biggest source of UB that we've probably had in Cub has been, like, initialization probleMs.
sentences.zh: 而最大的问题，也就是我们在 CUB 中可能遇到的最大的未定义行为来源，是初始化问题。

sentences.en: And that's largely been requirements change.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上是因为需求发生了变化。

sentences.en: When Cub was originally written,
sentences.zh: 当 CUB 最初编写时，

sentences.en: it was largely designed to work only with plain old data types and with things that it could assume could be left uninitialized or not zero-initialized because there was a cost to it.
sentences.zh: 它主要设计为仅适用于普通旧数据类型（POD），以及那些可以假设保持未初始化或不进行零初始化的类型，因为那样做有成本。

sentences.en: It was only later on as Cub evolved and Cub became the back end for Thrust in particular that the requirements had to change and that Cub then had to really support, you know,
sentences.zh: 直到后来，随着 CUB 的演进，特别是当 CUB 成为 Thrust 的后端时，需求不得不改变，CUB 必须真正支持，你知道，

sentences.en: arbitrary user-defined types.
sentences.zh: 任意用户定义的类型。

sentences.en: And at that point where, you know, like, all of the places where we just assumed that everything was int-like, you know, became a problem.
sentences.zh: 在那一点上，我们假设所有东西都是 int 类型的那些地方，就成了问题。

sentences.en: Or, like, another good example would be the fact that Cub defaults to 32-bit indexing, which has caused, you know, some amount of pain over the years.
sentences.zh: 或者，另一个很好的例子是 CUB 默认使用 32 位索引，这在过去几年里造成了一些痛苦。

sentences.en: But, like, recent versions of Cub now fully support 64-bit size and offset types, or we internally choose, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，CUB 的最新版本现在完全支持 64 位大小和偏移类型，或者我们在内部进行选择，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, we check what kind of size type you pass in.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们检查你传入的大小类型。

sentences.en: We can dispatch to an implementation that can handle large offsets.
sentences.zh: 我们可以分发给能够处理大偏移量的实现。

sentences.en: It will do an efficient thing, and it will do a correct thing.
sentences.zh: 它会执行高效的操作，并且会执行正确的操作。

sentences.en: Where did you work before NVIDIA?
sentences.zh: 你在加入 NVIDIA 之前在哪里工作？

sentences.en: And wait, we've got to let these guys finish their chicken nuggets.
sentences.zh: 等等，我们得让这些人吃完他们的鸡块。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And also, too, we haven't said, or you both haven't said.
sentences.zh: 还有，我们还没说，或者你们俩还没说。

sentences.en: Where you're based, because we, this is the first time we've ever had four NVIDIAs at once.
sentences.zh: 你们在哪里办公，因为这是我们第一次同时有四位 NVIDIA 员工。

sentences.en: Jared, we peaked at three.
sentences.zh: Jared，我们之前最多只有三个。

sentences.en: And so now we've got four.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有四个了。

sentences.en: But we're in the Netherlands right now.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在在荷兰。

sentences.en: A quattro.
sentences.zh: Quattro（四驱/四人）。

sentences.en: A quattro.
sentences.zh: 四人份。

sentences.en: He said that's a quattro in case, in case, that's an NVIDIA joke if you missed that, folks.
sentences.zh: 他说那是 Quattro，以防万一，如果你们没听懂的话，各位，那是个 NVIDIA 的梗。

sentences.en: But yeah, tell us where you're based, because we're not in America right now.
sentences.zh: 但说真的，告诉我们你们在哪里办公，因为我们现在不在美国。

sentences.en: I mean, both of us are basically now the German team at CCCL.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们俩现在基本上是 CCCL 的德国团队。

sentences.en: Or, no.
sentences.zh: 或者，不。

sentences.en: The Europe team?
sentences.zh: 欧洲团队？

sentences.en: At Cup.
sentences.zh: 在 CUB。

sentences.en: At Cup, let's say.
sentences.zh: 在 CUB，我们就这么说吧。

sentences.en: So, for the record, I'm based in Austria, which is no longer part of Germany.
sentences.zh: 郑重声明，我在奥地利办公，奥地利不再是德国的一部分了。

sentences.en: You know, there have been times, but that has been long ago, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，曾经有过那样的时期，但那是很久以前的事了，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm based in Austria, fully remote, working there for the CCCL team, maintaining Cup, Frost, and Lipku++.
sentences.zh: 我在奥地利完全远程办公，为 CCCL 团队工作，维护 CUB、Thrust 和 Libcu++。

sentences.en: Plus, I actually do live in the countryside, like, in a very small town, 1,700 inhabitants.
sentences.zh: 另外，我确实住在乡下，在一个非常小的镇上，只有 1700 名居民。

sentences.en: I lived in the mountains.
sentences.zh: 我住在山里。

sentences.en: The sound of the music, you know, like, the woman, like, dancing, singing on the hills, that's true.
sentences.zh: 《音乐之声》，你知道，那个女人在山上跳舞唱歌，那是真的。

sentences.en: What Bryce said about the sound of music is the most American thing that you could think about of Austria, but it's entirely true.
sentences.zh: Bryce 关于《音乐之声》的说法是你能想到的关于奥地利最美国化的想法，但它完全是真的。

sentences.en: Like, just last weekend, we organized the baptism of my son, and we went there in litterhosen and those shirts, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，就在上周末，我们为我儿子举办了洗礼，我们穿着皮裤和那种衬衫去了，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, as you would see in the movie.
sentences.zh: 就像你在电影里看到的那样。

sentences.en: So, that's not a lie.
sentences.zh: 所以，那不是谎言。

sentences.en: I actually watched the movie with my wife a couple years ago.
sentences.zh: 我几年前确实和我妻子看过那部电影。

sentences.en: For the first time?
sentences.zh: 第一次看？

sentences.en: For the first time, right?
sentences.zh: 第一次看，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's not a thing that we Austrians know a lot about, right?
sentences.zh: 因为这不是我们奥地利人很了解的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: There are better movies to watch.
sentences.zh: 有更好的电影可以看。

sentences.en: That is the only thing that America does.
sentences.zh: 那是美国唯一做的事情。

sentences.en: Exactly, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错，绝对是。

sentences.en: So, we figured we have to finally watch that, and it's actually a nice movie.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想我们终于得看一看，它其实是一部不错的电影。

sentences.en: It's well done, and it shows beautiful pictures of my country.
sentences.zh: 制作精良，而且展示了我祖国美丽的画面。

sentences.en: There's that one song where she's spinning around on the hilltop.
sentences.zh: 里面有一首歌是她在山顶上旋转。

sentences.en: Very beautiful.
sentences.zh: 非常美。

sentences.en: Very beautiful.
sentences.zh: 非常美。

sentences.en: Can you sing any of the songs?
sentences.zh: 你会唱里面的任何歌吗？

sentences.en: No, he's never.
sentences.zh: 不，他从来不会。

sentences.en: He's seen it once.
sentences.zh: 他只看过一次。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, no.
sentences.zh: 很遗憾，不会。

sentences.en: I'm not a good singer.
sentences.zh: 我不是个好歌手。

sentences.en: I also can't do, like, traditional dances or, like, mountain communication, you know, with big horns or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我也不会跳传统舞蹈，或者像山地通讯那样，你知道，用大号角之类的东西。

sentences.en: No, I'm not skilled in this.
sentences.zh: 不，我不擅长这个。

sentences.en: Here's a little ADSP, you know, inside knowledge.
sentences.zh: 这里有个 ADSP 的内部消息。

sentences.en: I mean, Bryce probably doesn't know this either.
sentences.zh: 我是说，Bryce 可能也不知道这个。

sentences.en: I have three sisters, and when I was younger, my mother, a massive Sound of Music fan, massive musical fan,
sentences.zh: 我有三个姐妹，当我年轻的时候，我母亲，一个《音乐之声》的超级粉丝，音乐剧的超级粉丝，

sentences.en: she would torture the four children that she had by making us perform songs from the Sound of Music.
sentences.zh: 她会折磨她的四个孩子，强迫我们表演《音乐之声》里的歌曲。

sentences.en: So, we would all have to line up in the living room and sing.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们都得在客厅排成一排唱歌。

sentences.en: Her favorite was the final song where they do the goodbyes in different languages.
sentences.zh: 她最喜欢的是最后一首歌，他们在里面用不同语言说再见。

sentences.en: Adieu to you and you and you and you.
sentences.zh: 再见，你，还有你，你，和你。

sentences.en: So long, farewell, I'll be just saying adieu.
sentences.zh: 再见，永别了，我这就说声再见。

sentences.en: Adieu, adieu to you and you and you.
sentences.zh: 再见，再见，你，还有你，你，和你。

sentences.en: And then you'd have to, like, flip and flat.
sentences.zh: 然后你还得，你知道，翻跟头。

sentences.en: I'm pretty sure that's either child abuse or forbidden by the Geneva Convention.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定那要么是虐待儿童，要么是被日内瓦公约禁止的。

sentences.en: I appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: I feel seen.
sentences.zh: 我感觉被理解了。

sentences.en: Thank you, Bryce.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，Bryce。

sentences.en: Because we all didn't like it.
sentences.zh: 因为我们都不喜欢那样。

sentences.en: And my mother, I love you, Mom.
sentences.zh: 还有我母亲，我爱你，妈妈。

sentences.en: You're not listening to this because I know you don't find this podcast interesting.
sentences.zh: 你没在听这个，因为我知道你觉得这个播客没意思。

sentences.en: But if you, for some reason, end up listening to this, yeah, we never liked it.
sentences.zh: 但如果你因为某种原因最终听到了这个，是的，我们从来都不喜欢那样。

sentences.en: And we all, you told us that we had to do it as your children.
sentences.zh: 而且我们所有人都，你告诉我们作为你的孩子必须这样做。

sentences.en: But it wasn't really.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是真的。

sentences.en: All right, all right.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: That was the question that initially was asked before I interrupted to say, where are you guys based?
sentences.zh: 这就是在我打断说“你们在哪里办公”之前最初提出的问题。

sentences.en: So where did you work before you were at NVIDIA?
sentences.zh: 那么在加入英伟达之前，你在哪里工作？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So before I joined NVIDIA, I did a PhD at CERN, which is a particle physics facility.
sentences.zh: 在加入英伟达之前，我在欧洲核子研究中心（CERN）攻读博士学位，那是一个粒子物理研究机构。

sentences.en: It's actually the largeSt.
sentences.zh: 实际上它是最大的。

sentences.en: It has a name, usually.
sentences.zh: 它通常是有名字的。

sentences.en: It's in Switzerland, in Geneva.
sentences.zh: 它位于瑞士日内瓦。

sentences.en: And we have huge machineries.
sentences.zh: 我们有巨大的机械设备。

sentences.en: Like, we have an underground particle collider that's 27 kilometers in circumference.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们有一个周长27公里的地下粒子对撞机。

sentences.en: It's massive detectors there, like tens of thousands of tons of underground silicon that just measure particle collisions.
sentences.zh: 那里有巨大的探测器，就像数万吨重的地下硅设备，专门用来测量粒子碰撞。

sentences.en: And it's full of radiation and high-voltage equipment, liquid helium everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是辐射、高压设备和液氦。

sentences.en: And it's just awesome.
sentences.zh: 简直太棒了。

sentences.en: It was safer than working on Cub.
sentences.zh: 它比在Cub工作更安全。

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 问得好。

sentences.en: I think we also had, like, a good share of undefined behavior there.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在那里也遇到了不少未定义行为。

sentences.en: Maybe in the defense of CERN, like, you had to do appropriate trainings before you could go into dangerous areas.
sentences.zh: 也许为CERN辩解一下，在进入危险区域之前，你必须接受适当的培训。

sentences.en: When I started out at NVIDIA, it immediately left me into the code base, completely untrained and unprepared of the horrors that I would see there.
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始在英伟达工作时，我直接被扔进了代码库，完全没有经过培训，也没准备好面对我即将看到的那些恐怖景象。

sentences.en: How did you end up at NVIDIA?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么来到英伟达的？

sentences.en: Because Paul was saying that he was using CCCL before.
sentences.zh: 因为Paul之前说过他在用CCCL。

sentences.en: He was a contributor.
sentences.zh: 他是一位贡献者。

sentences.en: And then he found his way.
sentences.zh: 然后他找到了自己的路。

sentences.en: Hey, were you a similar path?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你走的是类似的路径吗？

sentences.en: Or, you know, CERN just gets you a job at NVIDIA?
sentences.zh: 还是说，在CERN工作就能直接让你在英伟达找到工作？

sentences.en: Like, what a...
sentences.zh: 这简直……

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: So, many years back, I spared a whole life story, right?
sentences.zh: 很多年前，我省去了一整段人生故事，对吧？

sentences.en: But I'm doing C++ for quite a long time.
sentences.zh: 但我写C++已经很久了。

sentences.en: And around 2019, I attended my first C++ comedy meeting.
sentences.zh: 大约在2019年，我参加了我的第一次C++喜剧会议。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: I thought you said comedy for a second.
sentences.zh: 我刚才有一瞬间以为你说的是喜剧。

sentences.en: Comedy.
sentences.zh: 喜剧。

sentences.en: What am I being called?
sentences.zh: 大家都在叫我什么？

sentences.en: They are funny.
sentences.zh: 他们很有趣。

sentences.en: They are funny.
sentences.zh: 他们很有趣。

sentences.en: Maybe that wasn't a misspell, right?
sentences.zh: 也许那不是拼写错误，对吧？

sentences.en: So, I went to a comedy meeting and I fell in love with the language before.
sentences.zh: 总之，我去参加了一个喜剧会议，在那之前我就爱上了这门语言。

sentences.en: I really liked it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢它。

sentences.en: I kind of, like, grew into the C++ community.
sentences.zh: 我算是成长于C++社区。

sentences.en: And when I was at CERN, I further developed my skills in C++ and eventually kind of, like, grew into high-performance computing, where we also did some cheapy GPU computing.
sentences.zh: 当我在CERN时，我进一步提升了C++技能，最终涉足了高性能计算领域，我们在那里也做了一些简单的GPU计算。

sentences.en: And when the PhD kind of ended, you know, you ask yourself, like, what job can I imagine?
sentences.zh: 当博士学位快结束时，你会问自己，我能想象什么样的工作？

sentences.en: What company could I see myself working for?
sentences.zh: 我能想象自己在什么样的公司工作？

sentences.en: I knew I didn't want to continue in academia.
sentences.zh: 我知道我不想继续留在学术界。

sentences.en: So, I wondered what kind of company, you know, is invested in the C++ community, cares about that language,
sentences.zh: 所以我思考什么样的公司会投资C++社区，关心这门语言，

sentences.en: probably does GPU and care about performance, and can maybe employ me in Austria, fully remote,
sentences.zh: 可能做GPU相关工作，关心性能，并且能让我在奥地利全职远程办公，

sentences.en: because I wanted to move back from Switzerland, because my wife and me were about to start a family.
sentences.zh: 因为我想从瑞士搬回去，我和妻子当时正准备组建家庭。

sentences.en: And that didn't leave a lot of options there, right?
sentences.zh: 那里的选择并不多，对吧？

sentences.en: So, I figured NVIDIA was a natural choice that could combine all these interests and provide a nice place to work for.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为英伟达是一个自然的选择，它能结合我所有的兴趣，并提供一个不错的工作环境。

sentences.en: And didn't I, uh, we met for, like, the second or third time when I came to CERN to give a talk.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们不是在我去CERN做演讲时见过面吗，大概是第二次或第三次？

sentences.en: And then I was like, we gotta hire this guy.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，我们一定要雇佣这家伙。

sentences.en: And then I was like, I just, like, poked people on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 然后我就在推特上戳了戳大家。

sentences.en: Was that time during the podcast and you mentioned that you had gone to CERN?
sentences.zh: 那是播客期间你提到你去过CERN的时候吗？

sentences.en: Yes, that was, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是那时候。

sentences.en: And I just, uh, well, Bernhard gave...
sentences.zh: 我只是，嗯，Bernhard给了……

sentences.en: That means you've worked here for less than five years, probably, like, three or four?
sentences.zh: 这意味着你在这里工作不到五年，大概三四年吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, probably.
sentences.zh: 是的，大概吧。

sentences.en: Is that accurate?
sentences.zh: 准确吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I started NVIDIA one and a half years ago.
sentences.zh: 哦，我是一年半前加入英伟达的。

sentences.en: Okay, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的，没错。

sentences.en: So, so, there's actually, there's an even better part of the story, which is that when I went to CERN, um, I, I went there to give a talk.
sentences.zh: 其实这个故事还有更好的一部分，就是当我去CERN做演讲时，

sentences.en: And then, uh, the, like, some group of people at CERN organized, I think an intervention is probably the best way to describe it.
sentences.zh: CERN的一群人组织了一场——我觉得用“干预”来形容最贴切——

sentences.en: Where they took me into a room with a bunch of different CERN users and they were like, hey, we really care about reflection.
sentences.zh: 他们把我带进一个房间，里面有一群不同的CERN用户，他们说，嘿，我们真的很关心反射。

sentences.en: Can you get on board with caring about reflection, too?
sentences.zh: 你能加入我们，一起关心反射吗？

sentences.en: And, uh, I, uh, and, like, everybody gave a little presentation about, like, how they were using reflection, why reflection was important.
sentences.zh: 然后每个人都做了一个简短的演示，关于他们是如何使用反射的，以及为什么反射很重要。

sentences.en: And I remember you gave a presentation.
sentences.zh: 我记得你做了一个演示。

sentences.en: Yours was, everybody's presentation was good.
sentences.zh: 你的演示，每个人的演示都很好。

sentences.en: Yours was better than everybody else's.
sentences.zh: 但你的比其他所有人的都好。

sentences.en: And, uh, I was, and I was,
sentences.zh: 然后，我当时……

sentences.en: I actually was convinced by that meeting and I went out of that meeting and I went back and I went to all the C++ powers that be at NVIDIA and I was like, reflection,
sentences.zh: 我确实被那次会议说服了，我离开会议后，回去找了英伟达所有负责C++的大佬们，我说，反射，

sentences.en: we gotta make it a priority.
sentences.zh: 我们必须把它作为优先事项。

sentences.en: We should, uh, we should focus some effort on it.
sentences.zh: 我们应该投入一些精力。

sentences.en: And, uh, yeah, so, so you, you convinced me that we should care about reflection.
sentences.zh: 所以，是你让我相信我们应该关心反射。

sentences.en: And I was like, and we should also hire Bernard because he's, he's really good.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，我们还应该雇佣Bernhard，因为他真的很棒。

sentences.en: We gotta have him.
sentences.zh: 我们必须得到他。

sentences.en: Before we hand the mic back to Bernard, this is real bad because what a lot of listeners just heard is if you invite Bryce to your corporation,
sentences.zh: 在把麦克风交回给Bernhard之前，这真的很糟糕，因为很多听众刚才听到的是，如果你邀请Bryce去你的公司，

sentences.en: you can then potentially get a job at NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 你就有可能在英伟达得到一份工作。

sentences.en: I mean, well, if you can, if you can, if you invite me to come to your corporation and then you ambush me and convince, they didn't ambush me to be fair.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你邀请我到你的公司，然后伏击我并说服我——公平地说，他们并没有伏击我。

sentences.en: I was very happy to meet with him, but if you stage an intervention and try to convince, if you convince me of something, I mean, that's pretty, you make, you make a,
sentences.zh: 我很高兴见到他，但如果你策划了一场干预并试图说服我，如果你能说服我，我的意思是，那真的很……你做了一个，你做了一个……

sentences.en: you make a compelling presentation.
sentences.zh: 你做了一个令人信服的演示。

sentences.en: A presentation is the way to my heart.
sentences.zh: 演示是通往我心灵的途径。

sentences.en: A good slide deck is the way to my heart.
sentences.zh: 好的幻灯片是通往我心灵的途径。

sentences.en: I will tell you that.
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你。

sentences.en: Let's hand the mic back to Bernard.
sentences.zh: 让我们把麦克风交回给Bernhard。

sentences.en: So, uh, I have, I have like an awful lot of thoughts in my, in my head.
sentences.zh: 所以，我脑子里有很多想法。

sentences.en: Now, I know one that like, or whether I should like publicly speak about it, but since, uh, like, uh, reflection finally got standardized and in C++ 26,
sentences.zh: 现在，我知道有一个，或者说我是否应该公开谈论它，但既然反射终于在C++ 26中标准化了，

sentences.en: I think I can let Bryce in on some of the background.
sentences.zh: 我想我可以让Bryce了解一些背景。

sentences.en: Of, of, of, of why we locked him up in this room.
sentences.zh: 关于为什么我们要把他锁在那个房间里。

sentences.en: And the backstory was that CERN founded this open source program office and they wanted to have like a popular figure from the C++ community to speak there.
sentences.zh: 背景是CERN成立了这个开源项目办公室，他们想找一位C++社区的知名人士去演讲。

sentences.en: But CERN also has a very big interest in reflection as a feature because CERN develops this C++ interpreter.
sentences.zh: 但CERN对反射作为一项功能也非常感兴趣，因为CERN开发了这个C++解释器。

sentences.en: And that kind of like depends on generating matter information on C++ code.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上依赖于生成C++代码的元信息。

sentences.en: And CERN is actually pushing for reflection as a C++ feature, I think as early as 2005.
sentences.zh: 而且CERN实际上早在2005年就开始推动反射作为C++的一项功能了。

sentences.en: Like some people showed me papers like before C++ 11 where CERN was proposing reflection.
sentences.zh: 有些人给我看了C++ 11之前的论文，当时CERN就在提议反射了。

sentences.en: So, uh, when one of my supervisors kind of got in contact with Bryce to have him speak at that event, I already made the decision that after the PhD, I'm going to,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我的导师联系Bryce让他参加那个活动时，我已经决定博士毕业后，

sentences.en: I'm going to apply at NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 我要申请英伟达。

sentences.en: And I told him and my supervisor told me, look, we're going to have Bryce here.
sentences.zh: 我告诉了他，我的导师告诉我，看，我们要请Bryce来。

sentences.en: And one of our priorities would be to just make Bryce believe that reflection is an absolute killer feature.
sentences.zh: 我们的首要任务之一就是让Bryce相信反射是一个绝对的杀手级功能。

sentences.en: And he should make sure that every, every power that NVIDIA has should just push for reflection to get into the standard.
sentences.zh: 他应该确保英伟达拥有的每一份力量都应该推动反射进入标准。

sentences.en: And by the way, Bernhard, if you want to impress Bryce, maybe he can put in a good word to get higher than NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，Bernhard，如果你想给Bryce留下深刻印象，也许他能美言几句让你进入英伟达。

sentences.en: So you do the presentation in that room in front of Bryce and you make a good impression and convince Bryce that we want to have reflection in the standard.
sentences.zh: 所以你在那个房间里当着Bryce的面做了演示，留下了好印象，并说服了Bryce我们希望将反射纳入标准。

sentences.en: And boy, I was so nervous.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我当时太紧张了。

sentences.en: I couldn't sleep for weeks because I know my whole life and the life of CERN depended on the 20-minute presentation.
sentences.zh: 我好几周睡不着觉，因为我知道我的一生和CERN的未来都取决于那20分钟的演示。

sentences.en: I was scared shit.
sentences.zh: 我吓坏了。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Shouldn't say that, right?
sentences.zh: 不该这么说，对吧？

sentences.en: No, that's all right.
sentences.zh: 不，没关系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How long has the explicit tag been put on our podcast?
sentences.zh: 我们的播客加上“成人内容”标签有多久了？

sentences.en: So one of the, one of the things that actually came out of that presentation indirectly is that the reflection suffered, I think,
sentences.zh: 所以，那个演示间接产生的一个结果是，我认为反射在早期草案中，

sentences.en: in some of the earlier drafts from having not the strongest example.
sentences.zh: 因为没有最强有力的例子而受损。

sentences.en: A lot of people are making fun of it as like, oh, you can't do anything with this reflection.
sentences.zh: 很多人嘲笑它，说，哦，你用这个反射什么也做不了。

sentences.en: You can just do like enum to string.
sentences.zh: 你只能做枚举转字符串之类的。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons is that like the current reflection capability, you don't have a way to inject functions yet.
sentences.zh: 原因之一是目前的反射能力，你还没有办法注入函数。

sentences.en: Like, right, it's a static reflection only.
sentences.zh: 没错，它只是静态反射。

sentences.en: You don't have a way to like introduce new functions.
sentences.zh: 你没有办法引入新函数。

sentences.en: So it does, to some degree, limit what you can do.
sentences.zh: 所以它在某种程度上限制了你能做的事情。

sentences.en: But there was a very simple example that when one of the uses that y'all had at CERN was using reflection for reordering the fields of like a struct,
sentences.zh: 但有一个非常简单的例子，你们在CERN时使用反射来重新排列结构体的字段，

sentences.en: like packing or doing like array of struct, destructive array.
sentences.zh: 比如打包或者做结构体数组、数组结构体。

sentences.en: And that example I found very, very motivating.
sentences.zh: 那个例子我觉得非常有启发性。

sentences.en: And so I put that into a couple of talks and then I convinced the reflection authors, I think through Andre, that they should put it into their paper.
sentences.zh: 所以我把它放进了几次演讲中，然后我说服了反射的作者们，我想是通过Andre，让他们把它放进论文里。

sentences.en: And I would like to believe that that example is one of the best motivating examples.
sentences.zh: 我愿意相信那个例子是最好的激励性例子之一。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons, I'd like to think that's one of the reasons why we got reflection.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我们最终获得反射的原因之一。

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: That is a great, it is a great origin story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很棒的起源故事。

sentences.en: A great NVIDIA origin story for, for Brian.
sentences.zh: 一个很棒的Brian加入英伟达的起源故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: That is fantastic.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Who should, who should we?
sentences.zh: 我们应该让谁来？

sentences.en: We should get Kuhn on the mic here just for a sec because we mentioned your name earlier.
sentences.zh: 我们应该让Kuhn上麦说两句，因为我们之前提到了你的名字。

sentences.en: And Kuhn is the genesis, is the reason.
sentences.zh: Kuhn是起源，是原因。

sentences.en: You were the one that came up with Sean Perry.
sentences.zh: 你是那个提出Sean Perry的人。

sentences.en: It might be like you're, you're.
sentences.zh: 可能就像你……

sentences.en: We're going to get Sean Perry t-shirts.
sentences.zh: 我们要去买Sean Perry的T恤了。

sentences.en: We're going to have.
sentences.zh: 我们要有……

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: We are going to make, we are going to make, I, you know, I, I told Connor a couple days ago, I was thinking about making ADSP t-shirts, but you know, just a t-shirt that says ADSP,
sentences.zh: 我们要制作，我们要制作，你知道，我几天前告诉Connor，我在考虑制作ADSP T恤，但你知道，只是一件写着ADSP的T恤，

sentences.en: I didn't feel like it would be enough, but we're going to get t-shirts that have the parrot parrot on it, but with Sean's face.
sentences.zh: 我觉得还不够，但我们要制作印有鹦鹉的T恤，但要换上Sean的脸。

sentences.en: Here's a, this is coming from the folks that took five years to get you stickers.
sentences.zh: 这是那些花了五年时间才给你弄到贴纸的人说的话。

sentences.en: And it's not like we had the idea three months ago and it took us three months.
sentences.zh: 而且并不是我们三个月前才有这个想法，然后花了三个月。

sentences.en: We've been talking about stickers for like four of the five years of this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们在这个播客的五年里，大概有四年都在谈论贴纸。

sentences.en: I will execute quicker on this.
sentences.zh: 我会在这件事上执行得更快。

sentences.en: Anyways, intro, well, I mean, technically we don't need to introduce Coon because you were on the podcast almost a year ago or two years ago.
sentences.zh: 总之，介绍一下，嗯，我的意思是，技术上我们不需要介绍Kuhn，因为你一两年前就上过这个播客了。

sentences.en: Only one time.
sentences.zh: 只有一次。

sentences.en: Only one year.
sentences.zh: 只有一年。

sentences.en: Why'd you do two?
sentences.zh: 你为什么做两次？

sentences.en: Oh, for two episodes.
sentences.zh: 哦，因为有两集。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because you were at the table and that got diced, sliced and diced up as we do on ADSP because otherwise it wouldn't be a weekly podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 因为你当时在桌子旁，那段内容被切碎了，就像我们在ADSP上做的那样，否则它就不会是一个每周播出的播客了。

sentences.en: But what?
sentences.zh: 但是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, there were two recordings.
sentences.zh: 是的，有两次录音。

sentences.en: Were there two recordings?
sentences.zh: 有两次录音吗？

sentences.en: We recorded twice last year.
sentences.zh: 我们去年录了两次。

sentences.en: Or here, you explain.
sentences.zh: 或者在这儿，你来解释一下。

sentences.en: Here, take the mic and introduce yourself in case we have some new listeners since a year ago.
sentences.zh: 来，拿着麦克风做个自我介绍，以防有些听众是这一年才开始听我们节目的。

sentences.en: Shame on you for not going back to the backlog and listening all 200 episodes since you started listening.
sentences.zh: 你们这些从开始听节目到现在，还没回去把那200期往期节目都听一遍的人，真该感到羞愧。

sentences.en: We need those.
sentences.zh: 我们需要那些播放量。

sentences.en: And also, too, right before we give Coon the mic, we've recently discovered that like the
sentences.zh: 还有，在把麦克风交给Coon之前，我们最近发现，那个

sentences.en: Steve Jobs saved Sean Perrin episode is like the sixth, the most popular Sean episode.
sentences.zh: “Steve Jobs拯救了Sean Perrin”那一期，算是Sean系列里排名第六、最受欢迎的一期。

sentences.en: And like, I don't even think it's in the top 100 episodes.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得它甚至都没进前100名。

sentences.en: If we don't ask for much, listeners, we don't ask for much.
sentences.zh: 听众朋友们，我们要求的不多，真的不多。

sentences.en: What I'm asking is that you all go to your podcast player.
sentences.zh: 我只是请求大家打开你们的播客播放器。

sentences.en: You don't have to listen to it.
sentences.zh: 你们不必真的去听。

sentences.en: Just go back, download it from the archive and then erase it and mark it as played.
sentences.zh: 只要回去从归档里下载一下，然后删掉并标记为已播放就行。

sentences.en: We need it to be in like the top 10 because it's not okay that it's not in the top 100.
sentences.zh: 我们需要它进入前十名，因为它没进前100名实在说不过去。

sentences.en: Anyways, over to Coon.
sentences.zh: 总之，交给Coon吧。

sentences.en: Introduce yourself for those that didn't listen a year ago.
sentences.zh: 给那些去年没听过节目的听众做个自我介绍。

sentences.en: And maybe tell us about this year's, you know, C++ under the sea experience.
sentences.zh: 顺便跟我们聊聊今年“海底C++”（C++ under the sea）的体验。

sentences.en: And also, how did Sean Perrin come to you?
sentences.zh: 还有，Sean Perrin这个名字是怎么来的？

sentences.en: Because you're now a part, you were already a part of the lore of ADSP.
sentences.zh: 因为你现在已经是ADSP传说的一部分了，虽然你之前也算。

sentences.en: But now you're really going to be a part of the lore because Sean Perrin, that's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 但现在你真的成了传说的一部分，因为Sean Perrin这个梗太天才了。

sentences.en: Okay, so, yes, my name is Coon and I'm from Belgium.
sentences.zh: 好的，我是Coon，来自比利时。

sentences.en: And, well, this is actually my third episode because in the first episode I was in, it was actually recording by Tristan.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这其实是我第三次上节目，因为我第一次参与的那期，其实是Tristan录的。

sentences.en: I had a question on CPP OnSea last year.
sentences.zh: 去年在CPP OnSea上我提过一个问题。

sentences.en: My memory is so bad that, yes, we had the episode, I think it was at CPP North, where you had given, or you didn't give.
sentences.zh: 我的记性太差了，对，我们录过那一期，我想是在CPP North，你当时提问了，或者说你没提问。

sentences.en: Tristan whipped out his cell phone, recorded your question.
sentences.zh: Tristan掏出手机，录下了你的问题。

sentences.en: I believe it was about unique count and a parallel implementation of that and a possibility of the implementation.
sentences.zh: 我记得是关于唯一计数（unique count）以及它的并行实现，还有实现的可能性。

sentences.en: He played that for me at CPP North and then we responded to that.
sentences.zh: 他在CPP North给我放了那段录音，然后我们做了回应。

sentences.en: And then we met you here later at last year's edition.
sentences.zh: 后来我们在去年的会议上见到了你。

sentences.en: I totally had forgotten that backstory.
sentences.zh: 我完全忘了那段背景故事了。

sentences.en: It was, so when you said three, it wasn't two times at C++ under the sea.
sentences.zh: 所以当你说是三次时，并不是指在“海底C++”录了两次。

sentences.en: It was one time at C++ under the sea.
sentences.zh: 是在“海底C++”录了一次。

sentences.en: This is now the second and third overall because Tristan's recording of your voice at CPP North.
sentences.zh: 现在这是总共第二次和第三次，因为Tristan在CPP North录了你的声音。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错，绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, you're very much a part of the lore now.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你现在确实是传说的一部分了。

sentences.en: You've technically recorded at two different conferences.
sentences.zh: 你严格来说是在两个不同的会议上录过音。

sentences.en: How many people can we say that about?
sentences.zh: 有多少人能做到这一点？

sentences.en: I do not know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: You would know.
sentences.zh: 你应该知道。

sentences.en: You have the data.
sentences.zh: 你有数据。

sentences.en: I mean, basically just speakers, I think, because they're the folks that go to different conferences.
sentences.zh: 我想基本上只有演讲者吧，因为他们才会去参加不同的会议。

sentences.en: Anyways, back to you.
sentences.zh: 总之，回到你身上。

sentences.en: What did you think about this conference?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这次会议怎么样？

sentences.en: And you got any new, deeply insightful questions for us about the podcast?
sentences.zh: 对于我们的播客，你有什么新的、深刻的问题吗？

sentences.en: Feedback?
sentences.zh: 反馈？

sentences.en: Complaints?
sentences.zh: 抱怨？

sentences.en: Grievances?
sentences.zh: 不满？

sentences.en: Putting Kuhn on the spot.
sentences.zh: 让Kuhn当场表态。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't have any questions for the moment, but yeah, the parrot thing, well, just, I am now, I have a second daughter now.
sentences.zh: 目前还没什么问题，但是，关于Parrott这个梗，嗯，我刚有了第二个女儿。

sentences.en: And as things go, I can make a lot of dad jokes now.
sentences.zh: 随着生活的发展，我现在能讲很多“老爸笑话”了。

sentences.en: So Sean Parrott.
sentences.zh: 所以就有了Sean Parrott。

sentences.en: Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 恭喜你。

sentences.en: Also, is this a recent second daughter?
sentences.zh: 另外，第二个女儿是最近出生的吗？

sentences.en: February.
sentences.zh: 二月份。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 恭喜。

sentences.en: Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 恭喜。

sentences.en: So, that's why I'm making a lot of dad jokes now, and that was one of them that came to mind.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么我现在讲很多老爸笑话，那也是我当时想到的一个。

sentences.en: So, what did you think about the conference this year?
sentences.zh: 那么，你觉得今年的会议怎么样？

sentences.en: It was good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: I learned a lot about CUDA as well, so that was great to get some more insight on that.
sentences.zh: 我也学到了很多关于CUDA的知识，能深入了解这些真的很棒。

sentences.en: And, well, hearing Sean speak, of course, has also been a highlight.
sentences.zh: 当然，听Sean演讲也是一大亮点。

sentences.en: And getting to know the parrot library.
sentences.zh: 还有了解Parrott库。

sentences.en: It's funny, because some of the things I already also started implementing in our library, just because of the ease of use, to have a simple function to call, to have a sum,
sentences.zh: 很有趣，因为其中一些东西我已经开始在我们的库中实现了，仅仅是因为它使用起来很方便，有一个简单的函数调用就能求和，

sentences.en: instead of having to call, std, accumulate, and so on.
sentences.zh: 而不是非得调用std::accumulate之类的。

sentences.en: So, having this simple interface is something that really can help for colleagues, and just to have less code to make less mistakes.
sentences.zh: 所以，拥有这种简单的接口对同事们真的很有帮助，代码少了，犯错的机会也就少了。

sentences.en: So, that's really nice to see.
sentences.zh: 所以看到这个真的很棒。

sentences.en: I mean, this is amazing, folks.
sentences.zh: 伙计们，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: Dad jokes is what brought Sean Parrott into existence.
sentences.zh: 正是“老爸笑话”让Sean Parrott这个梗诞生了。

sentences.en: And you've got to understand, this is going to be a part of our lives now for years to come.
sentences.zh: 你们得明白，这在未来几年里都将是我们生活的一部分。

sentences.en: I mean, apparently there may be t-shirts being made.
sentences.zh: 我是说，显然可能还会有人制作T恤。

sentences.en: Sean is here.
sentences.zh: Sean就在这儿。

sentences.en: He gave a keynote, the opening keynote of the conference, and we got approval from him, because we don't want to abuse Sean's name like that.
sentences.zh: 他做了会议的开幕主题演讲，我们还征得了他的同意，因为我们不想滥用Sean的名字。

sentences.en: But he thought it was hilarious.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得这太搞笑了。

sentences.en: And, yeah, so now it's a part of our lives.
sentences.zh: 所以，现在它成了我们生活的一部分。

sentences.en: Dad jokes brought this name to you.
sentences.zh: 是老爸笑话把这个名字带给了你。

sentences.en: And, yeah, the dot sum, I mean, there's a conversation to be had at a later date about API design and the importance of an ergonomic and intuitive interface.
sentences.zh: 还有那个dot sum，关于API设计以及符合人体工程学和直观接口的重要性，我们以后还可以再聊。

sentences.en: Because I've had conversations with folks that don't necessarily think that that's enough to be a compelling thing.
sentences.zh: 因为我曾和一些人交流过，他们不一定认为这足以成为一个令人信服的理由。

sentences.en: And that's not all that Parrott is.
sentences.zh: 而且Parrott不仅仅只有这些。

sentences.en: That people believe that a better interface is not sufficient for a library to succeed?
sentences.zh: 有人认为更好的接口不足以让一个库成功？

sentences.en: A little bit, yeah.
sentences.zh: 有一点吧，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, with some asterisks.
sentences.zh: 我是说，带点保留意见。

sentences.en: But, you know, you always talk about the 10x difference to switch to a language.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，人们总是谈论切换到某种语言需要10倍的提升。

sentences.en: I don't know what the multiplier that you need to switch to a library.
sentences.zh: 我不知道切换到一个库需要什么样的倍数。

sentences.en: But I've heard the, quote, if it's just an improvement, an interface change, that's not enough.
sentences.zh: 但我听说过这种说法：如果仅仅是改进，只是接口上的改变，那是不够的。

sentences.en: But Parrott is not.
sentences.zh: 但Parrott不仅仅是这样。

sentences.en: What Parrott, the key selling feature of Parrott is that Parrott is maximally lazy.
sentences.zh: Parrott的关键卖点在于它极其懒惰（maximally lazy）。

sentences.en: And that means that Parrott is asynchronous by default and does fusion by default, both of which are the huge pain points of Thrust today.
sentences.zh: 这意味着Parrott默认是异步的，并且默认进行融合（fusion），这两点都是Thrust目前最大的痛点。

sentences.en: So the major pain points of Thrust are overcome almost immediately by Parrott.
sentences.zh: 所以Thrust的主要痛点几乎被Parrott立即克服了。

sentences.en: Cheers, Sean.
sentences.zh: 干杯，Sean。

sentences.en: But wait, well, let's say goodbye to Coon.
sentences.zh: 等等，我们先跟Coon道个别。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你。

sentences.en: This is your third appearance.
sentences.zh: 这是你第三次出镜了。

sentences.en: There's got to be a fourth, fifth, and sixth now down the road.
sentences.zh: 以后肯定还会有第四、第五、第六次。

sentences.en: And we're about to talk to Sean Parrott, which, you know, it's like right in the middle.
sentences.zh: 我们马上要和Sean Parrott谈谈，这正好在中间，

sentences.en: It's Sean Parrott.
sentences.zh: 是Sean Parrott。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So the name of the Parrott, which is the graphic signifier, not logo, of my library, has now been named by Coon because he has two daughters, a second daughter recently.
sentences.zh: 所以Parrott这个名字，也就是我库的图形标识（不是Logo），现在是由Coon命名的，因为他有两个女儿，最近刚有了第二个。

sentences.en: We should explain.
sentences.zh: 我们得解释一下。

sentences.en: NVIDIA has one team, one org, and one logo.
sentences.zh: NVIDIA只有一个团队，一个组织，一个Logo。

sentences.en: So there are no other logos.
sentences.zh: 所以没有其他Logo。

sentences.en: Some things do have graphic signifiers.
sentences.zh: 有些东西确实有图形标识。

sentences.en: I did on Wednesday, the day before this library was open source, I did spend an hour trying to get the icon of my library to be the Parrott.
sentences.zh: 周三，也就是这个库开源的前一天，我花了一个小时试图把库的图标改成Parrott。

sentences.en: Graphic signifier.
sentences.zh: 图形标识。

sentences.en: No, the icon of the GitHub repo.
sentences.zh: 不，是GitHub仓库的图标。

sentences.en: But it is within the NVLabs organization.
sentences.zh: 但它是在NVLabs组织下的。

sentences.en: And I determined after three different LLMs, an hour of like being gaslit.
sentences.zh: 在试了三个不同的LLM，被折磨了一个小时后，我放弃了。

sentences.en: It's like, oh, you just need to change the markdown, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 它们就像是说，哦，你只需要改一下markdown，巴拉巴拉。

sentences.en: So if the org sets it to be so that you cannot change the icon, you cannot change the icon.
sentences.zh: 所以如果组织设置了你不能更改图标，你就真的改不了。

sentences.en: Anyways, thank you, Coon, for being on.
sentences.zh: 总之，谢谢Coon来参加节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for Sean Parrott.
sentences.zh: 谢谢Sean Parrott。

sentences.en: We hope, I don't know, are we going to be back next year?
sentences.zh: 我们希望，我不知道，我们明年还会回来吗？

sentences.en: Maybe?
sentences.zh: 也许吧？

sentences.en: If we're back next year, hopefully you'll be here.
sentences.zh: 如果我们明年回来，希望你也能在。

sentences.en: And yeah, thanks for coming on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你来参加。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And with that, we will transition to not Sean Parrott, but Sean Parent.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们要过渡到另一位Sean，不是Sean Parrott，而是Sean Parent。

sentences.en: Be sure to check these show notes either in your podcast app or at adspthepodcaSt.com for links to anything we mentioned in today's episode,
sentences.zh: 请务必查看播客应用中的节目说明，或访问adspthepodcast.com获取我们今天提到的所有内容的链接，

sentences.en: as well as a link to a GitHub discussion where you can leave thoughts, comments, and questions.
sentences.zh: 以及GitHub讨论区的链接，你可以在那里留下想法、评论和问题。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoyed and have a great day.
sentences.zh: 希望你喜欢，祝你愉快。

sentences.en: Low quality, high quantity.
sentences.zh: 低质量，高产量。

sentences.en: That is the tagline of our podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们播客的口号。

sentences.en: That's not the tagline.
sentences.zh: 那不是口号。

sentences.en: Our tagline is chaos with sprinkles of information.
sentences.zh: 我们的口号是：充满混乱，撒点信息。
